_work.title: Thomas Norton — Ordinal of Alchemy (c. 1477): Manuscripts and 1652 Printed Plates
_work.blurb: The Ordinal of Alchemy (Ordinal of Alchimy) composed by the Bristol alchemist Thomas Norton c. 1477, the most important verse treatise on alchemy in Middle English. Written in rhyming couplets, the Ordinal describes the philosophical and practical stages of the Great Work through seven chapters, from the election of the alchemist to the perfection of the Stone. The work survives in seventeen manuscripts and was first printed with engraved plates in Elias Ashmole's Theatrum Chemicum Britannicum (1652).

entries.title: Master and Pupil — Ordinal of Alchemy Illumination, BL Add MS 10302
entries.commons_file: File:1477 thomas norton the ordinall of alchymy master and pupil.jpg
entries.summary: Illuminated manuscript page from BL Add MS 10302 (1477) depicting a master — likely George Ripley, Norton's claimed teacher — orally transmitting alchemical knowledge to a pupil identified as Thomas Norton. One of the earliest known English alchemical illustrations. Norton's insistence that the art must be learned from a true adept, not from books alone, is a major theme of Chapter I: the pupil's worthiness is tested through patience, secrecy, and philosophical preparation.

entries.title: Portrait of Thomas Norton (1433–1513) — from the Ordinal Manuscript
entries.summary: Portrait of English alchemist and poet Thomas Norton (d. 1513) from a contemporary manuscript of his Ordinal of Alchemy (BL Add MS 10302). Norton was a member of Parliament for Bristol and a gentleman alchemist who composed the Ordinal c. 1477. He claimed to have achieved the Great Work under the tutelage of George Ripley, though his manuscript of the Stone was allegedly stolen by a servant of his rival, the Duchess of Clarence.

entries.title: Figure 5 from Norton's Ordinal — Theatrum Chemicum Britannicum (1652)
entries.summary: Figure 5 from Thomas Norton's Ordinal of Alchemy as printed in Elias Ashmole's Theatrum Chemicum Britannicum (London, 1652) — one of the five engraved plates that accompanied the first printed edition. This figure is the most widely reproduced of the Ordinal's printed images and illustrates a later stage of the Great Work sequence. Ashmole's 1652 anthology is the most important English collection of alchemical verse.

entries.title: Theatrum Chemicum Britannicum — Title Page (1652)
entries.summary: Title page (A1r) of Elias Ashmole's Theatrum Chemicum Britannicum (London, 1652), the first major printed anthology of English alchemical verse. It gathered works by Thomas Norton, George Ripley, John Gower, Geoffrey Chaucer, John Lydgate, and others alongside Norton's Ordinal. Digitized from the University of Pennsylvania Schoenberg Center collection.

entries.title: Theatrum Chemicum Britannicum — Engraved Frontispiece, Wellcome L0012615
entries.commons_file: File:E. Ashmole, "Theatrum chemicum britannicum", 1652 Wellcome L0012615.jpg
entries.summary: Engraved frontispiece from the 1652 first edition of Ashmole's Theatrum Chemicum Britannicum, engraved by R. Vaughan. From the Wellcome Collection rare books holdings (catalog L0012615). The frontispiece establishes the scholarly and antiquarian authority Ashmole brought to the project — he framed English alchemical verse as a national heritage deserving systematic preservation.

entries.title: Early Alchemical Laboratory — Theatrum Chemicum Britannicum, Wellcome L0006176
entries.commons_file: File:Elias Ashmole. Theatrum chemicum britannicum Wellcome L0006176.jpg
entries.summary: Illustration from Ashmole's 1652 Theatrum Chemicum Britannicum depicting an early alchemical laboratory, showing furnaces, alchemical apparatus, and workspace as described in Norton's Ordinal and Ripley's Compound of Alchymy. From the Wellcome Collection rare books digitization project (L0006176). Licensed CC BY 4.0.

entries.title: Theatrum Chemicum Britannicum Leaf O2r — Astrology Page, Wellcome L0030725
entries.commons_file: File:E. Ashmole, Theatrum Chemicum Britannicum Wellcome L0030725.jpg
entries.summary: Leaf O2 recto (page 91) of Ashmole's 1652 Theatrum Chemicum Britannicum, noted as relating to astrology. From the Wellcome Library rare books collection (L0030725). Ashmole was himself a practicing astrologer in addition to his alchemical interests, and the Theatrum Chemicum Britannicum reflects the close relationship between alchemy and astrology in the English learned tradition. Licensed CC BY 4.0.

entries.title: The Operations of the Laboratory Inspired by the Great Masters — Wellcome L0004316
entries.commons_file: File:The Operations of the Laboratory inspired... Wellcome L0004316.jpg
entries.summary: Engraving from Ashmole's 1652 Theatrum Chemicum Britannicum titled 'The Operations of the Laboratory inspired by the Great Masters,' depicting alchemical laboratory practice in idealized form. The inscription links practical laboratory work to spiritual or intellectual inspiration from the tradition's masters — Norton, Ripley, Chaucer — whose verse fills the anthology. From the Wellcome Library rare books collection (L0004316). Licensed CC BY 4.0.

entries.title: The True Alchemical Laboratory — Theatrum Chemicum Britannicum, Wellcome L0004317
entries.commons_file: File:The True Alchemical Laboratory. Wellcome L0004317.jpg
entries.summary: Engraving from Ashmole's 1652 Theatrum Chemicum Britannicum depicting 'The True Alchemical Laboratory,' showing an idealized alchemical workspace — the 'true' laboratory being distinguished from the corrupt, merely mercenary laboratory of those who pursue only material profit. This distinction between the philosophical and the commercial alchemist is a key theme in Norton's Ordinal. From the Wellcome Library rare books collection (L0004317). Licensed CC BY 4.0.

entries.title: Theatrum Chemicum Britannicum — Upper Cover Binding, King George III Copy (BL 239.k.6)
entries.commons_file: File:Theatrum Chemicum Britannicum; containing severall poeticall pieces of our famous English philosophers, ... - Upper cover (239k6).jpg
entries.summary: Upper cover of the King George III copy of Ashmole's Theatrum Chemicum Britannicum (BL 239.k.6), featuring an 18th-century English armorial panel binding in brown calf tooled in gold. From the British Library's Digitised Bookbindings collection, ex libris King George III. The King's Library copy passed to the British Museum (and thence the British Library) in 1823. Licensed CC0.
